title: Privilege escalation through com_users batch task
short_summary: Privilege escalation through the Joomla com_users batch task.
summary: Joomla CMS 4.0.0 through 5.4.5 and 6.0.0 through 6.1.0 were affected by an improper access check in the com_users batch task. Authenticated attackers could abuse the batch flow to escalate privileges.

timeline.event: Reported to the Joomla Security Strike Team.
Confirmation of the issue and initial patch development.
Fixed in Joomla CMS 5.4.6 and 6.1.1 and CVE assigned.

title: Authenticated blind SQL injection in com_tags
short_summary: Authenticated blind SQL injection in Joomla com_tags.
summary: Joomla CMS 4.0.0 through 5.4.5 and 6.0.0 through 6.1.0 were affected by improper validation of order clauses in com_tags. Authenticated attackers could manipulate generated SQL and infer database contents through blind SQL injection.

timeline.event: Reported to the Joomla Security Strike Team.
First acknowledgment.
Confirmation of the issue and initial patch development.
Fixed in Joomla CMS 5.4.6 and 6.1.1 and CVE assigned.

title: Authenticated blind SQL injection in com_finder
short_summary: Authenticated blind SQL injection in Joomla com_finder.
summary: Joomla CMS 5.4.0 through 5.4.5 and 6.0.0 through 6.1.0 were affected by improperly constructed filter clauses in the com_finder search query. Authenticated attackers could influence the SQL query and infer database contents through blind SQL injection.

timeline.event: Reported to the Joomla Security Strike Team.
First acknowledgment.
Confirmation of the issue and initial patch development.
Fixed in Joomla CMS 5.4.6 and 6.1.1 and CVE assigned.

title: Authenticated blind SQL injection in SettingsIndividual.php
short_summary: Authenticated blind SQL injection in SettingsIndividual.php.
summary: In ChurchCRM 7.0.5, settings input handled by SettingsIndividual.php could be used by an authenticated user to influence a SQL query. The issue enabled blind SQL injection behavior that could expose sensitive database contents.

timeline.event: Report published to ChurchCRM and initial triage.
GitHub advisory published and CVE assigned.

title: Authenticated blind SQL injection in PropertyAssign.php
short_summary: Authenticated blind SQL injection in PropertyAssign.php.
summary: In ChurchCRM 7.0.5, property assignment handling in PropertyAssign.php exposed a blind SQL injection path for authenticated users. Attackers could infer database contents and potentially alter application data through injected SQL.

timeline.event: Report published to ChurchCRM and initial triage.
GitHub advisory published and CVE assigned.

title: Authenticated blind SQL injection in EventNames.php
short_summary: Authenticated blind SQL injection in EventNames.php.
summary: In ChurchCRM 7.0.5, event-name management in EventNames.php exposed SQL injection behavior to authenticated users with access to the affected configuration path. Successful exploitation could expose or modify ChurchCRM database records.

timeline.event: Report published to ChurchCRM and initial triage.
GitHub advisory published and CVE assigned.

title: Authenticated SQL injection in MemberRoleChange.php
summary: In ChurchCRM 7.0.5, authenticated users with group and role management privileges could inject SQL through the MemberRoleChange.php role update flow. Depending on deployment configuration, this could provide database read/write access and potential privilege escalation.

timeline.event: Report published to ChurchCRM and initial triage.
GitHub advisory published and CVE assigned.

title: Authenticated blind SQL injection in PropertyTypeEditor.php
short_summary: Authenticated blind SQL injection in PropertyTypeEditor.php.
summary: In ChurchCRM 7.0.5, property type editing in PropertyTypeEditor.php accepted authenticated input that could influence SQL statements. The issue could lead to database compromise, including data extraction or modification.

timeline.event: Report published to ChurchCRM and initial triage.
GitHub advisory published and CVE assigned.

title: Authenticated blind SQL injection in SettingsUser.php
short_summary: Authenticated blind SQL injection in SettingsUser.php.
summary: In ChurchCRM 7.0.5, user settings handling in SettingsUser.php exposed an authenticated blind SQL injection path. Attackers could infer and extract database data through timing-based or boolean blind SQL techniques.

timeline.event: Report published to ChurchCRM and initial triage.
GitHub advisory published and CVE assigned.

title: Second-order SQL injection via FundRaiserEditor.php
summary: ChurchCRM 7.1.2 and earlier allowed stored input from FundRaiserEditor.php to become executable SQL later in the fundraiser workflow. This second-order SQL injection could lead to database compromise once the malicious stored value was processed.

timeline.event: Report published to ChurchCRM and initial triage.
GitHub advisory published and CVE assigned.
